claims.text: The target alloy is equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
TOR-TILD's EAM references do not adequately represent or sample the many atomic configurations of liquid CoCrFeMnNi.
The proposed reference is an MLP trained on a diverse set of ab initio molecular-dynamics snapshots of the liquid.
The liquid training set will cover a broad range of local atomic environments.
Symmetry-function descriptors in the MLP will correctly capture the complexity of local configurations in the liquid.
Training on ab initio liquid configurations will reproduce the ab initio potential-energy surface more faithfully over a wide configuration space than the EAM reference.
More faithful reproduction of the potential-energy surface will improve reference–target phase-space overlap.
Improved reference–target phase-space overlap will reduce errors or mismatch along the thermodynamic-integration path.
The MLP reference will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch by approximately 50% relative to TOR-TILD's EAM references.
Free-energy differences obtained with the MLP reference will converge to within 5 meV/atom of direct ab initio free-energy calculations.
The proposed applicability range is from the melting temperature to approximately 200 K above it.
The comparison will cover both solid and liquid CoCrFeMnNi states.
The MLP's effectiveness may not transfer to other compositions or temperature ranges without adaptation.
An MLP trained as proposed may fail to generalize to all relevant configurations or may overfit.
Further training-set diversification and cross-validation may be required to eliminate thermodynamic-integration mismatch.
Failure to obtain an approximately 50% mismatch reduction or exceeding 5 meV/atom error against direct ab initio free energies will falsify the hypothesis.
